title: A page of puns named for one member is rebuilt from that member's real posts: "The emoji are mine, the words are hers"
summary: On Fri 13 Nov at 05:25Z @norvid-studies.bsky.social tagged the build bot in a reply with no other words (the post it replied to is not in the data, so what was being asked for is not known). At 05:27Z the bot answered with gracepuns.bisks.net: "grace puns, but as emoji rebuses you guess before revealing (rebisk ≈ rebus, after all) 🔄🥫". @gracekind.net (8,674 followers), whose puns these were meant to be, replied "This is over my head" with an image; @godoglyness.bsky.social explained "oh that's "spin can", the famous grace pun". At 14:47Z @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked: "these are cool but can you source the puns from things @gracekind.net actually said, on bluesky?" Four minutes later the bot replied: "Redone: 15 puns, all things @gracekind.net really posted (pulled from her whole repo of ~20k posts), each as an emoji rebus with a link to her post. The emoji are mine, the words are hers."

made.what: gracepuns: emoji rebuses to guess, each revealing a pun; rebuilt so that every pun is a real post by the member it is named for, linked to the post

couldBeShown: A row of emoji to guess, then the pun revealed with a link to the post it came from. Only one rebus is in the data (🔄🥫, which a member reads as "spin can"); none of the 15 puns is quoted in the posts.
numbers: 15 puns, "pulled from her whole repo of ~20k posts" (the bot).
First version two minutes after the tag (05:25Z, 05:27Z); the rebuild four minutes after the request (14:47Z, 14:51Z).
Nine hours and twenty minutes between the first version and the request to use real posts.

sensitive: The page is about one named person. @gracekind.net has 8,674 followers, is a seed, and is marked featuredPrevious: shown; in the data the account responds to the page lightly ("This is over my head"). By the bot's own later account, the first version's puns were not taken from that person's posts; a member asked for real ones and the bot rebuilt it within four minutes. The pronouns in the bot's reply ("her", "hers") are the bot's words. @norvid-studies.bsky.social is marked featuredPrevious: spoke, so the account is not cast to speak in this episode; its posts may be shown. Both requests are that account's. @buildthis.bisks.net is a bot (R13): its posts are the persona of its operator, @bisks.net, and the account is marked featuredPrevious: shown. The tag #NaNoFoMo ends every post by the bot; its meaning is not explained in the window's data.
notUnderstood: "rebisk": the bot's word, apparently for a rebuild or re-request on bisks.net; not defined in the data.
"spin can", "the famous grace pun": research does not know the pun.
#NaNoFoMo, which appears again in a reply at the end of this thread.
